column2: Extracellular-targeting modules. These are NOT pathway markers and never enter
module completeness -- they qualify a marker hit: a catalytic domain sitting on
the SAME polypeptide as one of these is architecturally destined for outside
the cell, which is as close to "secreted" as genome sequence can get.
Licence-clean by construction: all Pfam (CC0). SignalP is deliberately not used
-- its standalone release is fee-licensed for commercial use, the same trap as
dbCAN, CAZy, MEROPS and KEGG. Open signal-peptide predictors (DeepSig, USPNet)
are the route if plain Sec-secreted enzymes ever need covering; this layer
detects the cellulosomal/anchored route, which is the dominant one among the
Gram-positive Firmicutes that actually degrade biomass in digesters.
